children.required: Conditional (when the site country is USA: UNITED STATES)

children.label: Project/Performance Site Congressional District
children.help_text:
Enter the Congressional District in the format: 2 character State Abbreviation - 3 character District Number. Examples: CA-005 for California's 5th district, CA-012 for California's 12th district.

If all districts in a state are affected, enter "all" for the district number. Example: MD-all for all congressional districts in Maryland.

If nationwide (all districts in all states), enter US-all.

If the program/project is outside the US, enter 00-000.

To locate your congressional district, visit the Grants.gov web site.  Note it is likely that this field will be identical to the “Congressional Districts of Applicant” field provided elsewhere in this application.
children.required: Conditional (when the site country is USA: UNITED STATES)

SF-424 PROJECT/PERFORMANCE SITE LOCATION(S) FORM (4040-0010)

According to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, an agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to a collection of information unless it displays a valid OMB control number. The valid OMB control number for this information collection is 4040-0010. The time required to complete this information collection is estimated to average 14 minutes per response, including the time to review instructions, search existing data resources, gather the data needed and complete and review the information collection. The primary site is present. Other sites are optional; Street1, City and Country become required when an other-site entry exists. Their conditional requiredness is recorded in field text, not proven as executable behavior by parity.

DAT 1-07/2-08: State is active and required for a US country and inactive otherwise. DAT 1-08/2-08a: Province is inactive for US and active otherwise. DAT 1-10/2-10: ZIP is required with minimum nine characters for US; optional otherwise. Field constraints retain the general XSD bounds of 1..30.

DAT 1-11/2-11 requires congressional-district format **-***: six characters, hyphen third. The XSD provides bounds but omits this pattern. The plan preserves the DAT rule and records that source-layer difference.

DAT 2-03 lists maximum occurrences 1, while the Other Site group and XSD allow 299 sites with an independent UEI per site. The plan follows the repeated-site/XSD scope; this source discrepancy is recorded, not a source-policy approval.

DAT 3-1 Delete Entry removes the current other-site entry and is enabled only when more than one exists. DAT 3-2 Next Site requires a valid current entry and is disabled on the 299th entry. The current shared list supplies add/edit/remove capture, not the legacy current-entry-validity/Next Site workflow. These source interaction obligations remain explicit; navigation controls are not answer fields.

DAT 3-3 overflow attachment becomes active only after 299 other-site entries. Its help and source document purpose are retained; UUID upload-ID versus XML file-descriptor representation remains a later integration choice.

Proposed answer paths retain the existing SGG primary_site, additional_sites, submitting_as_individual, uei and additional_locations_attachment names at 1858f9a6f7052b101346eada88c9fba95b1ef208. Boolean checkboxes require the existing Yes/No XML projection; source enumeration is not a JSON boolean enum. Attachment value is omitted until a real uploaded-attachment UUID is available; no transport object is invented.

Demonstration answers are fictional, internally coherent examples rather than production identities. Realistic examples omit inapplicable Province from US addresses and do not contain attachment UUIDs without uploaded files. State-plus-Province and five-digit US ZIP probes remain separate negative/policy cases.
description: Project/performance site location definition and source plan for the primary site, up to 299 additional sites and the overflow attachment reference (FID723 v4.0). Reuses existing address, organization and attachment questions. The native preview is a library-side proof; SGG service and XML integration remain separate.
risks: Primary organization name is required unless the individual checkbox is checked, including an omitted choice. The DAT says this condition explicitly for the primary site; it is not silently generalized into a new unconditional requirement for other-site organization names.

The source is a checkbox with YesNoDataType XML values. Native entry captures checked as true and omits an unchecked optional checkbox; illustrative samples may contain false. Both draft states are admitted. Unticked versus absent versus No XML serialization remains an implementation decision, not a certified conversion.

Conditional activation/requiredness, US-specific ZIP minimum length and site-navigation limits require explicit behavior evidence; library-side tests do not establish SGG service or submission behavior. Static parity checks requiredness categories and supported bounds, not the truth of arbitrary conditional text.

Source DAT help for repeated-site fields sometimes says primary site. Retaining that wording makes provenance exact; clearer shared wording can be proposed with field-level evidence when mapping the question bank.

The plan preserves existing SGG congressional district character validation; the DAT states length/hyphen guidance and the XSD has no pattern. The stricter source-policy choice is pinned for review. Shared address rules, country values, US conditionals, 299-entry limit and attachment transport remain separate from completed local capture checks and require explicit SGG service/XML parity.
